Definition: gold, figuratively, something gold-colored (i.e. yellow), as oil, a clear sky
BiblicalUsage: zâhâb means gold, figuratively, something gold-colored (that is yellow), as oil, a clear sky. In Genesis 2:11 we read, "The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;". It appears again in Exodus 3:22: "But every woman shall borrow of her neighbour, and of her that sojourneth in her house, jewels of silver..."
TheologicalSignificance: zahab is gold, figuratively, something gold-colored (that is yellow), as oil, a clear sky, and I believe God does not use words carelessly, so this one does the work he gave it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
